page: Amazon Web Services r6in.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running on the x86_64 architecture with 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It lacks local instance storage, relying on network-attached EBS volumes, and does not include a GPU. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput and high memory bandwidth across data-heavy workloads. Multi-core performance is robust, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 123840.1 and a PassMark CPU score of 86579.42, ranking in the top tier. Extended instruction benchmarks and cryptographic processing reached 106437.4 and 111172.37 on PassMark respectively, driven by native AVX-512 and VAES vector extensions. Large-block memory bandwidth shows 332.96 GB/sec for read-only access and 135.67 GB/sec for write operations. Single-threaded performance sits within the middle 50% across stress-ng (1891.49) and Geekbench (1695.0), indicating that the system's strengths stem from aggregate core scaling rather than raw single-core clocks.

Application-level testing reveals strong metrics for data-layer infrastructure. The system recorded 107.01 million Redis SET operations per second and scored 29450.04 in PassMark database operations, reinforced by a static web serving throughput of 72.68 GB/sec. In LLM CPU inference tests, prompt processing reached 2833.8 tokens/sec on a 135M model and 195.57 tokens/sec on a 7B model, while text generation rates remained modest across all model sizes due to absence of GPU hardware accelerators.

The primary tradeoff of the r6in.32xlarge is its complete reliance on network storage for local I/O, which must be paired with high-performance EBS configurations to match the memory throughput. The instance delivers high resource density per node, optimizing costs for large deployments that require vast RAM capacities and high network throughput without paying for accelerator silicon. It is well matched for in-memory databases, distributed caches, real-time analytics engines, and large-scale relational database deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services r6in.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8375C processor, providing 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores at 3.5 GHz. It is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, and features 200 Gbps of baseline networking throughput. The instance includes no GPU acceleration and no local storage, requiring network-attached storage. Benchmarks show high multi-core compute capability, with top-tier PassMark CPU and encryption results accelerated by AVX-512 and VAES instructions, alongside uncached large-block read memory bandwidth of 332.96 GB/sec. Redis SET performance reached 107.01 million operations per second, confirming strong memory handling. The r6in.32xlarge suits in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, big data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
